documentation.purpose: A body text typography element for rendering paragraphs, inline text, and labels with design-system font styles.
documentation.usage:
Use the as prop to control the HTML element (span by default, also p, li, label, etc.).

Use size (x-small to large) and weight (default, strong, x-strong) to set typography.

Use color for semantic text colors.

Use boxColor when the text appears inside a colored container and needs a contextual color.

Use Heading for h1–h6 heading elements.

Use as='li' when the divider appears inside a list.

The padding prop controls spacing around the line, not the line thickness.

documentation.purpose:
A form label that associates visible text with an input element for accessibility.

Always use alongside form inputs like TextInput, Checkbox, Select, and Switch.
documentation.usage:
Always provide htmlFor matching the input's id, or use id on the Label with aria-labelledby on the input.

Use required prop to show an asterisk indicator.

Use variant='strong' for emphasized labels.

The Label automatically becomes visually disabled when its associated input is disabled — use data-label-ignore-disabled='true' on sibling containers (like action button groups) to prevent them from affecting the label state.

All props (direction, gap, align, justify, wrap, spacing) support responsive objects with breakpoint keys (base, xs, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl).

Gap accepts design token numbers or pixel strings.

Use as='span' for inline-flex contexts.

Use Grid when you need two-dimensional column/row layouts.

Exposed variant properties:

direction: row

align: flex-start, center, flex-end, stretch, baseline

justify: flex-start, center, flex-end, space-between, space-around, space-evenly

Text properties edit the exposed content.

Icon properties swap the native icon; Show properties control its visibility.

Coverage: partial.

Direction and explicit alignment/justification permutations exposed.

CSS stretch, space-around/space-evenly and wrapping/reverse-wrap require native layout parity; arbitrary responsive gap/dimensions are edited with native controls, not finite variants.

Source: https://github.com/Frontify/fondue/tree/ebcc9b8579a7f862f43a2732f5a5b9c3105e6796/packages/components/src/components/Flex/Flex.tsx

documentation.purpose:
A container with custom styled scrollbars that activates when content overflows its bounds.

Use when you need a scrollable region with consistent cross-browser scrollbar appearance.
documentation.usage:
Set maxHeight and/or maxWidth to define the scrollable viewport.

Use type='hover' (default) to only show scrollbars on hover, 'always' to always show them, or 'auto' to show only when overflowing.

Use scrollbarGutter='stable' to prevent layout shift when content changes between scrollable and non-scrollable.

Use showShadow to add an inset shadow at scroll edges.

documentation.purpose:

Use in forms where multiple independent options can be selected.
documentation.usage:
Always pair with a Label component for accessibility — connect them via matching id and htmlFor props, or use aria-labelledby. onChange receives the click event, not the new checked state (there is no onCheckedChange): to read or react to the state, control it with value plus your own state, e.g. const [checked, setChecked] = useState<boolean | 'indeterminate'>(false) and onChange={() => setChecked((previous) => previous !== true)}.

Use defaultValue for uncontrolled usage when the state isn't needed.

Use value='indeterminate' for partial selection states (e.g. select-all with mixed children).

Use RadioList when only one option from a group can be selected.

Use Switch for binary settings that take immediate effect rather than form submission.

documentation.purpose:
A group of radio buttons for single-choice selection from a list of options.

Use when users must pick exactly one option from a small, visible set.
documentation.usage:
Compose as RadioList.Root > RadioList.RadioButton.

Each RadioList.RadioButton requires a unique value prop.

Use RadioList.Root with asChild and a Flex container to customize the layout.

Pair each RadioButton with a Label for accessibility.

The root renders a role="radiogroup", which a Label htmlFor cannot name, so give the group an accessible name with aria-label or with aria-labelledby pointing at the group label, and associate hint or validation text with aria-describedby.

Use SegmentedControl for compact 2–5 option toggles inline with other controls.

Use Select for longer option lists that should be hidden in a dropdown.

Use for names, emails, URLs, search queries, and other single-line form inputs.
documentation.usage:
Use the simple TextInput for basic inputs, or compose TextInput.Root > TextInput.Slot for inputs with icon or button decorators.

TextInput.Slot accepts name='left' or 'right'.

Use status prop ('success', 'error', 'loading') to communicate validation state.

Always pair with a Label for accessibility.

Use Textarea for multi-line input.
documentation.properties:
status: loading
mode: default, hover, focus, disabled
content: value
slots: none
documentation.description:
A single-line text input field for collecting short text values.

Use for names, emails, URLs, search queries, and other single-line form inputs.

status: loading

content: value

Use EditableText for inline editing without a visible input border.

documentation.purpose: A range input for selecting a numerical value or range between a minimum and maximum.
documentation.usage:
Value is an array of numbers — use a single-element array for a single thumb, or two elements for a range slider.

Use defaultValue for uncontrolled or value + onChange for controlled. onChange fires during drag; onCommit fires only when the user releases.

Use minStepsBetweenThumbs to enforce a minimum gap in range sliders.

Always provide aria-label or aria-labelledby for accessibility.

recipes.name: SegmentedControl/Source states
limitations: Hug-width controls can resize natively; item count is arbitrary through duplication.
Responsive label clamp is represented at the 16px maximum.

documentation.purpose:
A compact control for selecting one of 2–5 mutually exclusive options.

Use it for view mode switches, layout changes, filter selections, or input choices where all options should remain visible and directly selectable.
documentation.usage:
Compose as SegmentedControl.Root > SegmentedControl.Item.

Each item requires a unique value prop.

Use defaultValue for uncontrolled usage or value + onValueChange for controlled.

Use hugWidth=false to stretch to container width.

The root renders a role="radiogroup", which a Label htmlFor cannot name, so give it an accessible name with aria-label or with aria-labelledby pointing at the Label, and associate hint or validation text with aria-describedby.

Use Tabs when switching also changes the visible content panel below.

Use RadioList or Select for longer option sets.
documentation.properties:

disabled: false, true
iconOnly: false, true
hugWidth: false, true

recipes.name: Notice/Source states
limitations: Message/action text and leading/dismiss icon visibility are native properties.
Arbitrary custom React action content is composed with the other native control assets.
Forced-colors media rendering remains in CSS.

documentation.purpose:
An inline alert banner for displaying feedback messages such as errors, warnings, success confirmations, or informational notices.

Use to keep users informed without interrupting their workflow by presenting clear, accessible feedback that stays visible until acknowledged.
documentation.usage:
Use variant to set intent (default, highlight, positive, danger, warning).

Use emphasis='strong' for high-visibility banners and 'weak' for subtle inline notices.

Provide an icon ReactNode to add a leading icon.

Provide an action ReactNode (typically a Button) for actionable notices.

Provide onDismiss to show a dismiss button.

Set role='alert' for errors that need immediate attention (e.g. a failed action the user just triggered); the default role='status' announces politely.

Children is the message content.

Use emphasis='strong' for high-visibility banners and 'weak' for subtle inline notices.

Provide an icon ReactNode to add a leading icon.

Provide an action ReactNode (typically a Button) for actionable notices.

Provide onDismiss to show a dismiss button.

Set role='alert' for errors that need immediate attention (e.g. a failed action the user just triggered); the default role='status' announces politely.

Children is the message content.

documentation.purpose:
A set of collapsible sections where each item can be independently expanded or collapsed.

Use when you need to organize large amounts of information into digestible sections, conserving space and improve scannability.
documentation.usage:
Always compose as Accordion.Root > Accordion.Item > Accordion.Header + Accordion.Content.

Each Accordion.Item requires a unique string value prop.

Use Accordion.Slot with name="action" inside Accordion.Header to place action buttons (e.g. edit/delete) on the right side of the header.

Use Accordion.Slot without a name for badge-style secondary content.

Add divider prop to Accordion.Content to show a separator between header and content if necessary based on the layout needs.

documentation.purpose:
A modal overlay that interrupts the user to present important content or require a decision.

Use for confirmations, forms, or detail views that need to be completed before continuing.
documentation.usage:
Compose as Dialog.Root > Dialog.Trigger + Dialog.Content.

Inside Dialog.Content use Dialog.Header, Dialog.Body, and Dialog.Footer for standard layout.

Always include Dialog.Title (can be screenReaderOnly) for accessibility.

Use Dialog.Description for additional context announced to screen readers.

Wrap cancel buttons in Dialog.Close to auto-close on click.

Use showUnderlay on Dialog.Content to dim the page behind the modal.

Use Flyout for non-blocking contextual panels instead.

documentation.purpose:

Use for lists of actions or navigation options that don't require value selection.
documentation.usage:

Use Dropdown.Group to group related items — provide a heading prop for labeled groups.

Use Dropdown.SubMenu > Dropdown.SubTrigger + Dropdown.SubContent for nested menus.

Use Dropdown.Slot with name='left' or 'right' inside Dropdown.Item to add icon decorators.

Use Dropdown.Shortcut inside Dropdown.Item to display the keyboard shortcut for actions that have one (e.g. 'K + E', '⌘ + N') and set aria-keyshortcuts on the matching Dropdown.Item; register the actual key listener in the consuming app.

Use emphasis='danger' on Dropdown.Item for destructive actions.

Use Select instead when users need to pick a value from a list.

documentation.purpose:
A dropdown for selecting a single value from a list of options.

Use Select.Combobox for searchable/filterable selection, and Select.Multiple or Select.Combobox.Multiple for multi-value selection.
documentation.usage:
Use Select for simple single-value selection.

Use Select.Combobox when users need to search or filter the options list.

Use Select.Multiple or Select.Combobox.Multiple for multi-value selection.

Place Select.Item (and Select.Group) inside <Select.Slot name='menu'>.

Items may be passed as direct children only when no other Select.Slot is used; as soon as you add a decorator (Select.Slot name='left' or 'right') or a clear button (Select.Slot name='clear'), direct-child items are ignored, so always wrapping them in the menu slot is the safe default.

Group options with Select.Group. onSelect on Select and Select.Combobox receives the selected value, or null when the selection is cleared; on the Multiple variants it receives the array of selected values.

Use Dropdown instead when items trigger actions rather than selecting a value.

Use indeterminateValues on Select.Multiple or Select.Combobox.Multiple when editing several records at once and an option applies to some of them but not all.

Those options render a dash instead of a checkmark and the trigger gains a '2 mixed' badge next to the selection badges.

Indeterminate values are purely visual and are never reported by onSelect.

Toggling an indeterminate item: clicking it sets it to selected and it is reported in the array passed to onSelect.

Clicking it again removes the selected state and it is omitted from the array passed to onSelect.

Important: the consumer must remove the value from indeterminateValues themselves once it has been selected, otherwise it shows as indeterminate instead of unselected after being deselected.

documentation.purpose:
A dropdown for selecting a single value from a list of options.

Use Select.Combobox for searchable/filterable selection, and Select.Multiple or Select.Combobox.Multiple for multi-value selection.
documentation.usage:
Use Select for simple single-value selection.

Use Select.Combobox when users need to search or filter the options list.

Use Select.Multiple or Select.Combobox.Multiple for multi-value selection.

Place Select.Item (and Select.Group) inside <Select.Slot name='menu'>.

Items may be passed as direct children only when no other Select.Slot is used; as soon as you add a decorator (Select.Slot name='left' or 'right') or a clear button (Select.Slot name='clear'), direct-child items are ignored, so always wrapping them in the menu slot is the safe default.

Group options with Select.Group. onSelect on Select and Select.Combobox receives the selected value, or null when the selection is cleared; on the Multiple variants it receives the array of selected values.

Use Dropdown instead when items trigger actions rather than selecting a value.

Use indeterminateValues on Select.Multiple or Select.Combobox.Multiple when editing several records at once and an option applies to some of them but not all.

Those options render a dash instead of a checkmark and the trigger gains a '2 mixed' badge next to the selection badges.

Indeterminate values are purely visual and are never reported by onSelect.

Toggling an indeterminate item: clicking it sets it to selected and it is reported in the array passed to onSelect.

Clicking it again removes the selected state and it is omitted from the array passed to onSelect.

Important: the consumer must remove the value from indeterminateValues themselves once it has been selected, otherwise it shows as indeterminate instead of unselected after being deselected.

documentation.purpose:
A hierarchical list of items and nested folders.

Supports keyboard navigation, single-select with a highlighted row or multi-select with cascading folder checkboxes (folders without loaded children are checkable as their own entity), optional drag-and-drop reordering, inline renaming, and async loading rows.
documentation.usage:
Compose with Tree.Root wrapping Tree.Item leaves and Tree.Folder nodes.

Each row needs a stable `id` and declares its content via anatomy parts: <Tree.Label> (plain text, required) plus optional <Tree.Icon> (rows render no icon otherwise), <Tree.Decorator> for passive badges/status icons hugging the label text (clicks bubble to the row; hidden while renaming), and <Tree.Action> for trailing controls (overflow menu, edit/delete; clicks do not bubble to the row).

For items the parts are direct children; for folders they go inside <Tree.FolderHeader>, and every other folder child is a nested row.

Render <Tree.Loading> as a child of a folder (or of Tree.Root for the top-level slot) to show a translated 'Loading…' row while async content is fetched.

Pass `multiSelect` for cascading checkboxes and `reorderable` to enable drag-and-drop; gate drops with an `accepts` predicate on Tree.Root or Tree.Folder, and tag draggable rows via the `tags` prop so the predicate can match by category instead of identity.

State is controlled: render from the latest `TreeChangeState` and persist it from `onChange`. `isSelected` is the unified selection prop — with `multiSelect` it checks the row's checkbox, without `multiSelect` it highlights the row, and either mode emits the updated flag via `onChange`.

In `multiSelect`, a folder with children derives its checkbox from its contents and ignores its own `isSelected`; a folder with no loaded children (empty, or collapsed while lazy-loading) is instead checkable as its own entity — `isSelected` is honored, `onSelectChange` fires on the folder, and it counts as one unit toward ancestor states.

When the children of a checked folder load later, the consumer has to carry the selected state over to the new items by passing `isSelected` to all of them.

documentation.purpose:
A drag-and-drop sortable list where users can reorder items.

Use when the order of items has semantic meaning and needs to be changed by the user.
documentation.usage:
Compose as OrderableList.Root > OrderableList.Item.

The order prop is a string array of item IDs that controls render order — always keep it in sync via onOrderChange.

Each OrderableList.Item requires a unique id prop.

Add OrderableList.DragHandle inside items for an explicit drag handle; omit it to make the entire item draggable.

Use OrderableList.ItemTitle and OrderableList.ItemDescription for standard content layout.

Add OrderableList.ItemAction for per-item action buttons.

Use when the user needs to select a specific date or date range.

DatePicker does not include its own trigger or popover — combine DatePicker.Input as the Flyout.Trigger and DatePicker (or DatePicker.Range) inside Flyout.Content for the standard pattern.

Dates are represented as plain objects { year, month, day } — not JS Date objects.

Use DatePicker.Range for range selection.

Pass disabledDates to grey out individual days.

Pass minMonth and/or maxMonth to bound month navigation — the previous/next-month controls disable once the bound month is reached.

Exposed variant properties:

disabled: false, true

isOpen: false, true

selected: , 2026-10-30

Text properties edit the exposed content.

Icon properties swap the native icon; Show properties control its visibility.

Coverage: partial.

Formatting is English sample; clear/change callbacks remain runtime.

Use for icon-only buttons, truncated text, or any UI element that benefits from a brief explanation.

documentation.usage:
Use AssetInput.Placeholder for the empty state, composing AssetInput.UploadInput and/or AssetInput.BrowseInput.

Use AssetInput.Root for the filled state, composing AssetInput.Preview (with one or more AssetInput.PreviewImage/AssetInput.PreviewIcon/AssetInput.PreviewLoading), AssetInput.Title, and AssetInput.Metadata wrapping one or more AssetInput.MetadataItem entries.

Control the open state with isOpen and onPress on AssetInput.Root, typically to toggle an attached Dropdown for asset operations.

Control the open state with isOpen and onPress on AssetInput.Root, typically to toggle an attached Dropdown for asset operations.

Exposed variant properties:

orientation: horizontal, vertical

isOpen: false, true

Text properties edit the exposed content.

Icon properties swap the native icon; Show properties control its visibility.

Coverage: partial.

This separate recipe composes the released AssetInput.Root+Preview+PreviewImage; existing PDF/icon AssetInput recipes are retained. orientation and isOpen are actual Root props.

Single-image preview uses object-fit:contain at 56px horizontal or 128px vertical.

Root width 360/280 is a documented sample container; vertical title/caret row 48px derives from the 16px caret and 16px padding.

Two-to-four-part image grids, loading states, missing-title/metadata layouts and text ellipsis are not enumerated here; arbitrary image URLs and onPress behavior stay in code.

Images are approved local example fixtures, not a screenshot of a component or page.

Replace the image fill for application content.

Native variants are static; source image loading, alternative-text accessibility, DOM sizing and browser events still require application/runtime verification.

children.name: intro
children.text: Your brand’s AI tools and agents find, organize, and create for you — right where you already work.

children.name: description
children.text: Keep every asset organized, even as your library grows. Set a rule once — say, when a file is uploaded, use AI to generate a description, translate it, and apply tags — and automations handle the rest. Combine a large variety of actions with OpenAI-powered or custom triggers to connect other AI tools and extend your workflows even further. The upkeep runs in the background, and no one has to think about it.
